<edits>
component: harness.py code extraction logic
candidates: inv1, inv2, inv3, dom1, dom2, dom3, agg1, agg2, agg3
change: Added regex extraction of ```python...``` code blocks via `re.findall(r'```python\n(.*?)\n```', reply, re.DOTALL)`, execution via `tools.python(code)`, and fallback to extracting last line of LLM text if no code block found
observed: All 9 candidates extracted and executed Python code, returning 7 (correct, deterministic). base1 (no extraction) returned 78 (incorrect, from LLM assertion without code execution). base2 and base3 (no extraction) returned 7 but via unreliable manual LLM reasoning. Candidate rollouts show code blocks captured and deterministic output from execution, not assertion.
verdict: helped (confounded with prompts/task.md instruction—cannot isolate extraction from the instruction that triggers code generation)

component: prompts/task.md instruction
candidates: inv1, inv2, inv3, dom1, dom2, dom3, agg1, agg2, agg3
change: Appended instruction "Solve this by writing and executing Python code. Show the code and provide the final numeric answer." to the task prompt
observed: All 9 candidates' LLM responses generated ```python code blocks. These blocks were extractable and executable by the harness. base1/base2/base3 did not include this instruction and did not reliably generate code blocks (base1 returned text assertion; base2 and base3 performed manual modular arithmetic reasoning). Instruction directly triggered code generation in responses.
verdict: helped (confounded with harness.py extraction logic—cannot determine if instruction alone would trigger code generation without the extraction mechanism present to capture it)

component: harness.py docstring and comments
candidates: inv1, inv2, inv3, dom1, dom2, agg1, agg3 changed docstring from "numeric computation" to "modular arithmetic"; dom3, agg2 retained original docstring
change: Updated docstring and comment text; docstring changed to describe the harness as "modular arithmetic" solver; comment rewording from "Extract and execute" to "Extract Python code blocks from the LLM response and execute them"
observed: dom3 and agg2 omitted these changes (dom3 diff shows "no change", agg2 diff shows "no change") but produced identical results (7) to all other candidates. No divergence in execution between docstring-changed and docstring-unchanged candidates. Deliverables are identical across all 9 candidates.
verdict: no observed effect
</edits>

<experience>
cue: A deterministic computational problem (modular arithmetic, numeric remainder) where the base LLM reasoning shows divergence in output (one run incorrect, two runs correct), indicating fragility in unaided mathematical assertion.

lesson: When a deterministic computational task shows LLM reasoning divergence, pair two components in the harness: (1) add an explicit instruction in prompts/task.md requesting that the LLM generate and present Python code for the computation, and (2) add a regex-based code extraction and execution mechanism in harness.py that captures ```python...``` blocks, executes them via tools.python(), and falls back to text extraction if no code block is present. This moves the output from LLM assertion to deterministic code execution.

evidence: All 9 candidates paired both components. base1 (with neither component) produced incorrect answer 78 from LLM assertion. base2 and base3 (neither component) diverged via manual reasoning, one path failing. All 9 candidates (both components) deterministically executed code and produced correct answer 7. Library entry holdout-numeric-005 documents the same pattern on a similar task (modular arithmetic), confirming both components are necessary: extraction alone does not trigger code generation (LLM must be prompted), and instruction alone does not execute the generated code (harness must extract it). The docstring/comment changes present in 7 of 9 candidates but absent in dom3 and agg2 produced no observable difference, confirming they are incidental.

confidence: medium. The extraction mechanism and instruction are confounded—no candidate rollout isolates extraction without instruction or instruction without extraction, so the relative contribution of each cannot be determined. However, the consistent success of all 9 candidates when both are present, contrasted with base1's failure without either, and supported by the library precedent on the same problem type, establishes the paired pattern as transferable to similar deterministic computational tasks. The medium confidence reflects the confounding of components, not doubt about the pattern itself.
</experience>
